options: The time stays the same however big the input is
The time grows in step with the size of the input
The time grows with the square of the input
check.explanation: O(n) is linear: double the input and the work roughly doubles. O(1) would stay the same, and O(n squared) would quadruple.
check.hint: n is the size of the input, and the work grows in proportion to it.

check.prompt: A loop inside another loop, each going over all n items, is usually which?
check.explanation: The inner loop runs n times for each of the n outer turns, so about n times n steps. That is why nested loops get slow so fast.
check.hint: Count the steps: n turns of the outer loop, each running the inner loop n times.

check.prompt: Binary search halves the data at each step. How does its time grow?
options: Logarithmically: doubling the data adds only one more step
Linearly, in step with the data
It does not depend on the data at all
check.explanation: Halving again and again reaches one item in about log n steps, so a million items need only about 20. That is far better than linear.
check.hint: Think about how many times you can halve a million before one item is left.
